transcript.answer: No, not any more. Context evals did run nightly in CI at first. PR #2463, merged 2026-10-02, added `.github/workflows/context-evals.yml`, which ran every night at 03:17 UTC and could also be started by hand. PR #2823, merged 2026-10-19, then removed that workflow. The evals now run from a developer machine with `scripts/context-evals/run.mjs` against the deployed lore-api, and nothing runs them on a schedule. The PR gave two reasons: the evals are experiments a person runs and writes up, and the unattended run had gone red three nights running (10-17, 10-18 and 10-19) on a single `demo-factory-todo` document that nobody read. The FR-9 text in `specs/1-lore-platform/spec.md` still describes a nightly GitHub Actions job. That text predates the removal and no longer matches the current state.

judgements.reason: The answer says no and that the evals ran nightly from 2026-10-02 via #2463 until they were later removed, which matches the gold answer; the extra detail does not contradict it.
